summary.title: A Workflow for Identifying Viable Crystal Structures with Partially Occupied Sites Applied to Solid Electrolyte: Cubic Li 7 La 3 Zr 2 O 12
summary.authors: Julian Holland; Tom Demeyere; Arihant Bhandari; Felix Hanke; Victor Milman; Chris-Kriton Skylaris
summary.executive_summary: This study addresses the lack of consensus regarding the ground state configuration of cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 (c-LLZO), a prominent solid electrolyte candidate. Previous experimental and theoretical works have failed to identify the stable structure due to the vast combinatorial space of possible Li site occupancies. The authors present a novel methodology to identify energetically favorable configurations by systematically generating and ranking all possible structures. The workflow begins by eliminating physically impossible structures where Li atoms overlap, using a minimum Li-Li distance constraint of 1.7 Å. This geometric constraint significantly reduces the configuration space by limiting the possible 24d:96h site ratios. Further reduction is achieved by removing symmetry-equivalent duplicates using local sensitive hashing (LSH), which scales linearly with the number of structures. The remaining unique structures are then energetically ordered using a machine learning model, specifically a multiple linear regression (MLR) trained on Density Functional Theory (DFT) data. The DFT calculations were performed using the ONETEP code with the PBE functional. The study finds that the lowest energy structures predominantly feature an 8:48 ratio of 24d to 96h site occupancy. Four structures are identified within 0.026 eV of the global minimum energy. The authors demonstrate that a large portion of previously reported structures in the literature may not be feasible or stable due to violating the minimum Li-Li distance constraint. The generated structures are made available in a public database to improve reproducibility and accuracy in future c-LLZO research. This work provides a robust framework for identifying viable crystal structures in materials with partially occupied sites, extending beyond c-LLZO to other ion conductors.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study addresses the lack of consensus regarding the ground state configuration of cubic Li7La3Zr2O12 (c-LLZO), a prominent solid electrolyte candidate. Previous experimental and theoretical works have failed to identify the stable structure due to the vast combinatorial space of possible Li site occupancies. The authors present a novel methodology to identify energetically favorable configurations by systematically generating and ranking all possible structures. The workflow begins by eliminating physically impossible structures where Li atoms overlap, using a minimum Li-Li distance constraint of 1.7 Å. This geometric constraint significantly reduces the configuration space by limiting the possible 24d:96h site ratios. Further reduction is achieved by removing symmetry-equivalent duplicates using local sensitive hashing (LSH), which scales linearly with the number of structures. The remaining unique structures are then energetically ordered using a machine learning model, specifically a multiple linear regression (MLR) trained on Density Functional Theory (DFT) data. The DFT calculations were performed using the ONETEP code with the PBE functional. The study finds that the lowest energy structures predominantly feature an 8:48 ratio of 24d to 96h site occupancy. Four structures are identified within 0.026 eV of the global minimum energy. The authors demonstrate that a large portion of previously reported structures in the literature may not be feasible or stable due to violating the minimum Li-Li distance constraint. The generated structures are made available in a public database to improve reproducibility and accuracy in future c-LLZO research. This work provides a robust framework for identifying viable crystal structures in materials with partially occupied sites, extending beyond c-LLZO to other ion conductors.

Research Context
Experimental and theoretical works have failed to uncover the ground state configuration of cubic Li7La3Zr2O12. Computational studies typically rely on an initial low-energy structure as a reference point. There is no consensus on the Li occupancy of c-LLZO in the literature. Previous studies often use experimental values as starting points for idealised unit cells. The range of predicted structures indicates disagreement about the ground state. Without knowing if structures are close to the ground state, properties may not be well described.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to find and rank all possible Li site occupancies for c-LLZO. The authors intend to produce all possible structures of a c-LLZO unit cell. They seek to ascertain if there is a significant energy difference in structure choice. The study hopes to elicit if structural properties like 24d:96h ratio indicate energy. The methodology aims to identify energetically favourable configurations of c-LLZO. The method is designed to be extended to other ion conductors.

Methodological Details
The total number of ways to populate 120 sites with 56 Li is approximately 7.4 × 10^34. A brute-force combinatorial method is unviable due to this large number. Structures with overlapping Li atoms are eliminated using a minimal Li-Li distance. The chosen minimal Li-Li distance is 1.7 Å. This distance is less than 2 times the ionic radius of a Li atom. The 48g site is neglected as it is not reported in most refinements. The crystal structure sites reported by Buschmann et al. are used as the framework. The total number of generated structures is approximately 2.3 × 10^8. Symmetry-equivalent duplicates are removed using local sensitive hashing (LSH). LSH optimizes pairwise comparison from O(N^2) to O(N). Only approximately 1% of structures are symmetrically unique. The configuration space is reduced to around 2 × 10^6 structures. DFT calculations were performed on 1235 single point structures. The first subset consisted of the 200 energetically lowest structures according to COMPASSIII. The second subset was a random selection of approximately 1000 structures. DFT calculations were performed with the ONETEP code. The PBE GGA exchange correlation functional was used. A kinetic energy cutoff of 830 eV was applied. A multiple linear regression (MLR) model was fitted to the DFT energies. Structures were represented by a frequency occurrence list of Li-Li interactions. Data were split into test and training sets with a 1:3 ratio.

Procedures And Architectures
All possible 24d permutations are generated for a given 24d occupancy. Directly neighbouring 96h sites are eliminated from consideration. Remaining 96h sites are populated such that no two nearest neighbours are occupied. An upper triangular connectivity matrix of the Li sub-lattice is constructed. The matrix is flattened and sorted to ensure uniformity. LSH is used to perform fast approximate similarity searches. The method is limited to comparison of monoatomic sub-lattices with predefined positions. The method was validated for 13:43 and 12:44 ratios. DFT calculations were performed on small subsets to fit the MLR model. The COMPASSIII forcefield was used to pre-select the lowest energy structures. ONETEP was used for DFT calculations with linear scaling. CASTEP on-the-fly generated pseudopotentials were used. Geometry optimisation calculations were performed on the final four structures. Broyder-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) was used for geometry optimisation.

Key Results
The MLR model achieved a correlation of 0.9996 on the test set. All structures occur within a range of 5.8 eV of the lowest energy structure. 19 out of the 20 lowest energy structures have a ratio of 8:48. The 19th lowest energy structure has a ratio of 9:47. The average energy for all structures is 1.47 eV higher than the ground state. The average energy for each ratio increases with increasing 24d occupancy. There is an energetic preference to avoid 24d occupation where possible. Four structures, all 8:48, are within 0.026 eV of the lowest energy structure. The four lowest energy structures have very similar atomic coordinates. All four lowest structures have the same 24d configuration. Only slight variations exist in the 96h configuration of the lowest structures. Geometry optimisation narrows the energy gap between the final four structures. A large proportion of experimental and theoretical literature structures are not feasible. The 96h to 24d transition yielded the lowest overall energy structure. This lowest energy structure was 0.58 eV lower than the single point minimum.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The methodology enables the isolation of low-energy structures for crystallographically predicted structures. Geometrical constraints from the methodology determine that many reported structures may not be feasible. The method can be extended to other ion conductors and partially occupied crystals. Providing all structures aims to improve accuracy and reproducibility in c-LLZO research. The study highlights that a large portion of literature structures are not reflective of real systems. The workflow provides a fast evaluation procedure for crystals with partially occupied sites.

Contradictions And Limitations
The energetic ordering procedure does not include entropic contributions. The study assumes a reasonable retention of ordering upon geometry relaxation. A large-scale energy prediction of geometry optimised structures is outside the scope. The LSH method is limited to monoatomic sub-lattices with predefined positions. The trade-off for increased speed is the high specificity of the method. COMPASSIII predicts a more pronounced separation of energies than ONETEP. The issue with COMPASSIII was considered too large to surmount in this paper. The choice of initial structure in previous studies was mostly for convenience. Coulombic forces alone are not sufficient to energetically order c-LLZO structures.

Claims
A significant portion of previously reported c-LLZO structures are not physically feasible due to Li-Li overlap. The study eliminates structures involving overlapping Li atoms. A minimal Li-Li distance of 1.7 Å is imposed. A large portion of literature structures may not be feasible. Some literature structures might be valid if dopants are considered. Future research should verify structures against this geometric constraint.
The 8:48 ratio of 24d to 96h site occupancy is energetically preferred. 19 of the 20 lowest energy structures have an 8:48 ratio. Average energy increases with increasing 24d occupancy. One of the lowest structures has a 9:47 ratio. This ratio should be prioritized in future computational studies.

Data And Code Availability
All structures generated are published in a freely accessible database. The database aims to improve accuracy and reproducibility in c-LLZO research. Scripts for symmetry checking are provided with the database.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The symmetry checking method was validated against ASE for 12:44 and 13:43 ratios. The same number of structures were produced using both methods. Including symmetry in the MLR model made a negligible difference. Geometry relaxation was tested on a small dataset of 20 structures. A negative correlation was found between distance moved and final energy.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the 24d:96h ratios that cannot exist without Li-Li interaction. Figure 2b shows the energy distribution of structures. Figure 3 shows the workflow to find the 4 final structures. Table 1 gives the number of structures for each 24d:96h ratio. Figure S3 compares DFT energies to COMPASSIII predictions. Figure S4 shows the energy of a Li Dimer with changing distance. Figure S5 plots MLR energies against space group order.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is a workflow to identify viable crystal structures with partially occupied sites. 2. The strongest evidence is the identification of four low-energy structures with an 8:48 ratio. 3. The future path is the extension of this method to other ion conductors.
